 Appearance:

 Order
This is fifth application filed under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.347/2021 registered at Police Station -Ambah, District - Morena (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 302, 304-B, 498A, 34 of IPC and under Sections 3/4 of The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Her First and third bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 28.08.2023 and 04.10.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.
Nos.12963/2025 and 40544/2025 respectively.
Her second bail application was dismissed on merits vide order dated26.07.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.16884/2024.
Her fourth bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to revive the prayers in terms of the custody period with Jabar Singh vide order dated16.06.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.22913/2025.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:298 2 MCRC-49816-2025 2.

As per prosecution story, the allegation against present applicant is that she along with co-accused subjected the deceased to cruelty for demand of Rs.2,00,000/- and when the demand was not fulfilled then, they poured kerosene oil on the deceased and set her on fire, as a result of which, the deceased died during treatment.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent.
She has been falsely implicated in this case.
Applicant is in custody since 17.10.2022.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.

The co-accused namely- Jabar Singh Tomar has already been enlarged on bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 30.08.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.
27335/2024 on the ground of period of custody and status of trial, under the similar set of facts and Guddi Devi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160943955/
1 allegations, therefore, the present applicant seeks parity.

sentences.text: She is having no criminal history.
Conclusion of the trial will

Applicant is the permanent resident of District Morena (M.P.), therefore,
there is no possibility of her absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make herself available as and when required.
Under these grounds, counsel for applicant prayed for bail.
3. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent/State as well as counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its dismissal.

4. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:298 3 MCRC-49816-2025 5.

Considering the above submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and also on the ground of parity, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lac Only)
with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
8. Certified copy as per rules.
